lead: the rack you built last winter holds exactly the tools three of them use. the rest have not noticed there is nothing of theirs in it, and you never said a word about who works here.
sun: you pay the sub, you have a key, your name is on the rota in the same handwriting as everybody else's. and from the stool at the end you could always see which of them was here for the work and which was here for the room. that was plain from where you sit years before the ones who left began leaving, and invisible to anyone standing in the middle of it.
moon: The Hand has no interest in waiting for a vote. the sorting arrives and within a fortnight there is an object on the wall built to the shape of it — a rack sized for three, a jig that assumes a particular pair of people. none of that was argued. it was made, and a made thing is not a position anybody can disagree with in a meeting.
pull: nothing was ever said out loud in that room. it was fitted, quietly, to the half of it that works, and the other half has been leaving for years without being told why.
tension: nothing you have done to that place is on any minute. so when somebody says the shed has changed, the sentence that follows is about the committee or the subs, and you are in the circle nodding. the ones who drifted out did not have a grievance to bring, because there was nothing said to bring one against — the bench simply stopped having a spot at it that was theirs, and they blamed the work getting harder.
cost: the half of that room that is actually working ends up equipped inside one winter, with nobody outvoted and nothing on record. the equipping is a verdict. it leaves your hands without a note attached, and the people it was not built around read the place as having gone cold and drift off somewhere else, still fond of you.

lead: it has been quoted at twenty-two arguments this year, always by whoever was already winning. the work went out under your name with nothing on it but what is there and nothing at all around it.
sun: that register has had your name on it since you were twenty-three and nobody has ever queried it. the work only exists because of where you sit: inside enough to have the real numbers, angled enough to notice that the trade divides into the ones doing the job and the ones with an arrangement, which everybody deep in it experiences as one profession with a bit of variation.
moon: it went where anyone can get it, with your name on the front and no guard on it — no membership condition, no version that stays inside the body. plain and true were the only two properties The Jewel built into it, and neither is armour. it was public inside a week of being finished, admired at once and defended by nobody, least of all you.
pull: you gave a whole trade an accurate picture of itself and wrote nothing on it about which half was which. it has been used as a knife by everyone except you.
tension: both sides cite it and both are entitled to. the numbers say what they say, and each side's reading of them is one you would have reached standing where they stand, so correcting either is endorsing the other. the word for you now is either detached or calculating. the second is nearer, and saying so in a room you are still on the register of is not available.
cost: the field ended with the account of itself that it uses, and it exists because you were near enough to the middle to have the material and far enough off to see the seam. nothing was fitted to it saying who it was for. the people it damaged signed your nomination papers, and the front of it has your name on it in the same size it always had.

lead: anyone can tell you where you belong — the body, the years, the number on the card. nobody in it, after two decades, could name one other thing about you that is true.
sun: the membership is not in question: subs paid, nineteen years, your name read out at the meeting with everybody else's. and from that seat you can see the body come apart into the ones holding it up and the ones being held, which is not visible from any chair nearer the middle. the seam has been plain to you for a decade and you are on the roll of the thing it runs through.
moon: the card answers the question and nothing else does. no faction has managed to count you as theirs, and you never refused one — The Veil left no register anywhere of what you think, and no fixed position was ever issued to you along with the membership. inside a place that has you documented, precisely, you cannot be located.
pull: the roll says where you are, and no other true sentence about you is on file anywhere. everyone stopped asking the second question years ago, because the first one had an answer.
tension: the ask, when a body divides, is to declare, and there is nothing in you to declare with — what you hold is a vantage, and allegiance was never part of the equipment. you get called cagey, or political, or a safe pair of hands. an outsider would be left alone with it. a member of nineteen years who cannot be placed reads as withholding, and the roll is exactly what makes it read that way.
cost: when a body divides it says both of its cases to you plainly, because no file on you exists to check against and no side to report you to. you are left holding the shape of a quarrel nobody else can see whole. what the record has of you is a number, a joining date and a subscription history, and the day you stop paying, that is all that stays.

lead: both halves came to you after the split, and both grips closed, and neither has opened since. the line the place came apart along is the one you named out loud at a meeting in your thirties.
sun: nobody has ever had to check whether you belong there — you were on the roll before either faction existed and you are still on it. you sat inside the work and slightly to one side of it, which is the one place the two intentions in one body were visible from, years before either had a name. you said so once, in a sentence, and everybody in that meeting remembers who said it.
moon: and then The Claws took hold of both sides. you carry the finance argument for one of them and the whole history of grievance for the other, both entire, neither shaded down to make room for the other. from outside it reads as somebody who will not commit. it is two loads carried at once, and carrying them is what makes you the slowest person in the fight.
pull: you named the seam a decade before it opened and you are holding both edges of it now. the fight will be over before you have finished being right about it.
tension: the side that lost dates the whole thing to your sentence, which is fair, and the side that won thinks you were with them all along, which is not. neither reading has room in it for the arrangement: two grips, both real, both costing you the same evenings. speed decides these. the faction that moved first took the room and the name, and you were still weighing two accurate cases when the vote happened.
cost: both factions still send you the thing they cannot put in writing, because you are the only route between them that has not been cut, and holding both cases whole is what keeps that route usable. by the time you can say which half of that place was load-bearing, the other half has already been running it for a year, and what you know arrives as history.
